analytic.title: Towards a new Schedulability Technique of Real-Time Systems based on Difference of Constraints System

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: In this paper a novel schedulability analysis technique of real-time systems is presented. The developed approach is based on the consideration of the reachability graph of the (untimed) underlying Petri net of the studied model. The schedulability analysis is then conducted in two steps. Once a feasible firing sequence (called occurrence sequence) is highlighted, this sequence is then described under an algebraic form of type Ax ≤ b. The particular features of matrix A lead to a bimonotone linear inequality system. A bimonotone linear inequality is a linear inequality with at most two nonzero coefficients that are of opposite signs (if both different from zero). Thus, deciding whether a firing sequence is schedulable or not takes the form of the solution of a single-source shortest path problem which can be polynomially solved via the Bellman-Ford algorithm.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: A real-time system can be defined as a system whose correctness depends not only on the logical result of computations, but also on the time at which the results are produced. Nowadays real-time systems become indispensable in our lives and can be found in avionics, automotive industry, medicine, telecommunication industry, mecatronics, space industry, etc. For this kind of systems, the response-time constraints must be imperatively respected and a missed deadline can generally lead to significant loss. Indeed, it must process information and produce its response within a specified time or it risks severe consequences, including system failure. To face their increasing complexity it becomes inevitable to develop formal methods allowing to handle their particularities. For such systems the process of verifying whether a sequence of operations (or tasks) completes without violation of timing constraints is referred to as schedulability analysis.

Petri nets (PN) [6] are recognized as an convenient tool for the modeling and the analysis of asynchronous, discrete event dynamic systems with concurrency. Proposed originally as a causal logic model explicitly neglecting time, they have been extended in order to meet the requirements of specific application areas. In particular for real-time systems [1], [9] PNs are extended with two time parameters representing a minimum and a maximum delay. The most used time model is the Merlin's one (TPN) associating a time interval to each transition of the net. For the model considered in this paper, namely P-time Petri Nets (P-TPN) [4], the timing constraints are attached to places and its firing rule P. Most of the analysis techniques of time models are based on enumerative approaches [1], [8] aimed at generating the set of all reachable markings and cannot be used to determine the end-to-end delay in task execution which is a key requirement for real-time systems analysis.

Tsai et al. [9] address the problem of real-time specifications schedulability regarding a set of imposed timing constraints. Their approach uses a PN model called Timing Constraint Petri Nets (TCPN). The proposed method relies on a three-steps analysis : specification modeling, reachability simulation and timing analysis. Although, TCPN possess a great expressive power, practicaly, it appears to be complicated to use. Inspired by the work of Tsai et al., Xu et al. [7] propose a compositional approach based on absolute and relative firing domains to reduce the complexity of schedulability analysis for time critical systems modeled by TPN. The authors proposed to separate timing properties from other behavioral properties. To overcome the state space explosion problem inherent to enumerative based techniques, Bernardi et al. [3] developed a structural performance analysis method for TPN. It uses linear programming techniques and is aimed at computing performance bounds to partially characterize the quantitative behavior of systems modeled by TPN by exploiting their structural properties. Recently, in [2] the author developed a method which exploits the equivalence between a particular behavior of the modeled system and a linear inequality system. This paper introduces a new schedulability analysis technique for real-time systems. It is based on the analysis of the set of feasible occurrence sequences of the underlying (untimed) PN of the P-TPN model considered. More precisely, the approach allows to check whether an occurrence sequence is schedulable in the associated P-TPN by solving a system of difference of constraints. Indeed, this sequence will be described under an algebraic form of type Ax ≤ b where matrix A has particular features leading to a bimonotone [12] linear inequality system.

The paper is organized as follows: a brief remainder of the basics of untimed Petri nets followed by a formal definition of P-Time Petri nets is realized in the next section. Section three deals with the schedulability analysis approach. Section four discusses the reachability problem of P-TPN based on the reachability graph of the underlying untimed Petri net. Finally, in the last section some conclusions are presented.

div.head: II. PETRI NETS A. Untimed Petri Nets [6]
div.p: A Place/Transition net (P/T net) is a structure N = (P, T, P re, P ost), where P is a set of m places; T is a set of n transitions. P re : P × T → N and P ost : P × T → N are the pre and post incidence functions that specify the arcs; C = P ost -P re is the incidence matrix. The preset and postset of a node X ∈ P ∪ T are denoted • X and X • . A marking is a vector M : P → N that assigns to each place of a P/T net a non-negative integer number of tokens, represented by black dots. M (p) is the marking of place p. A net system N ; M 0 is a net N with an initial marking M 0 . A transition t is marking enabled at M if M ≥ P re(•, t). A transition t enabled at M may fire, yielding the marking M = M +C(•, t). A marking M is reachable in N ; M 0 iff there exists a firing sequence σ such that M 0 [σ > M . The set of all markings reachable from M 0 defines the reachability set of N ; M 0 and is denoted R(N ; M 0 ). Finally, we denote P R(N ; M 0 ) the potentially reachable set, i.e., the set of all markings M ∈ N m for which there exists a vector

div.p: It holds that R(N ; M 0 ) ⊆ P R(N ; M 0 ). A Petri net having no directed circuits is called acyclic.

div.p: In a P-TPN, a transition sequence σ = t 1 t 2 . . . t s is said to be schedulable if all transitions in σ are schedulable in the given order. So, it exists a set of markings M 1 , M 2 , . . . , M s such that (M 0 t 1 M 1 t 2 . . . t s M s ) is a feasible sequence in the underlying net and t i , i ∈ {1, . . . , s} is schedulable under M i-1 . If at least one transition in σ is non schedulable then σ is non schedulable. In a P-TPN, the schedulability of a transitions sequence is verified with regard to the timing constraints associated with the model places. In the underlying PN of a P-TPN, denoted UPN, a marking is said to be reachable if there exists a firing sequence (M 0 t 1 M 1 t 2 . . . t s M s ), or simply an occurrence sequence δ = (t 1 t 2 . . . t s ) which leads to marking M s starting from the initial marking M 0 . The notation L(M 0 , M n ) will be used to denote the set of all possible feasible firing sequence in an UPN from M 0 to M n (L(M 0 ) will denote the set of feasible firing sequence of the UPN, starting from M 0 ). If a transition sequence is not an occurrence sequence in the UPN, it can't be schedulable in its associated P-TPN. Nevertheless, an occurrence sequence in the UPN is not necessarily schedulable in the associated P-TPN because of the timing constraints.
The following section addresses the schedulability analysis of an occurrence sequence.

div.head: A. Constraints Graph
div.p: Given a set of constraints with n + 1 variables the corresponding constraint graph is a weighted directed graph (V, E) where
div.formula: • V = {s 0 , v 0 , v 1 , v 2 . . . v n } (a set of nodes), • E = {(v i , v j )|x i -x j ≤ b k is a constraint } ∪ {(s 0 , v i )|i ∈ [0, n]} (a set of directed edges), • w(v i , v j ) = 0 if v i = s 0 , ∀j b k if x i -x j ≤ b k is a constraint.
div.p: Where w is a weight function, associated each edge with a weight and defined as: w : E → Q.

Informally speaking, each decision variable X i of the difference constraints system will be associated to a corresponding node v i of the constraints graph. The directed arcs will be deduced from the (x i -x j ≤ b k ) constraint and the unique source node s 0 will be associated with a 0-weight edge to each vertex v i ∈ V .
It is worth noticing that with this addition of node s 0 no negative-weight cycles will be introduced, so the shortest paths exist.
Thus a feasible solution for a system of difference of constraints amounts to finding the single source shortest path in the constraint graph in the following way:

div.p: A shortest path from node u to node v is then defined as any path p with weight w(p) = δ(u, v).
A negative weight cycle is a path: p = v 0 , v 1 , v 2 , . . . , v k subject to:

div.head: IV. SCHEDULABILITY AND REACHABILITY
div.p: In a P-TPN the reachability of a particular marking M n can be discussed in terms of schedulability of a firing sequence σ ∈ L(M 0 , M n ). Indeed, marking M n will be reachable if a schedule starting from M 0 and leading to M n exists. In the presented approach determining whether M n is reachable may required the analysis of all the possible firing sequences from M 0 to M n for the untimed underlying PN of the P-TPN considered.
The following theorem are recalled.
Theorem 3: [2] A marking M n is unreachable in a P-TPN if it is unreachable in its associated underlying untimed PN (i.e. its UPN).
Theorem 4: [2] It is decidable whether a marking M n in a P-TPN is reachable or not if L(M 0 , M n ) is a finite set.
Theorem 5: [10] Let N be an acyclic Petri net.

div.p: It is decidable whether a marking M n in a P-TPN is reachable or not if its underlying untimed PN is acyclic.

In [11] Ramachandran et al. proposed a net transformation procedure which convert a general Petri net into an acyclic one. Their basic idea is to expand the considered PN into multiple layers with the places of the n th layer forming the input for the (n + 1) th layer. Thanks to the developed approach, based on a net expansion scheme, the necessary and sufficient reachability condition stated for acyclic PN can be extended to any general Petri net.

Theorem 7: [11] In a general Petri net, a marking M n ∈ R(N ; M 0 ) if and only if there exists a positive integer α such that the state equation of the α-stage expanded Petri net M α,n = M α,0 + C α .y has a non-negative integer solution.

With M α,0 (resp. M α,n ) the initial (resp. the n th ) marking of the α-stage expanded Petri net and C α its incidence matrix. Intuitively, α can be seen as the net expansion factor and it represents the length of the firing sequences (i.e. the number of transitions) for which all the states can be fully obtained.
So, the following lemma has been stated. Lemma 1: [2] It is decidable whether a marking M n in a P-TPN is reachable or not.

Theorem 8: Let consider a marking M n in a P-TPN with L(M 0 , M n ) being a finite set. Let G σ be the constraints graph associated with the occurrence sequence σ. If ∀σ ∈ L(M 0 , M n ), G σ contains a negative-weight cycle, then marking M n is not reachable from M 0 in the associated P-TPN.

V. CONCLUSIONS Time represents a major issue in the analysis of real-time systems. Indeed, for such systems where all tasks are timeconstrained, this parameter does not affect only the system performances but also its correctness. Thus, an acceptable behavior depends not only on the order of the events but particularly on the time at which the results are produced and checking whether a sequence of events can complete in time is a crucial issue.

In this paper, a new schedulability analysis technique for real-time systems modeled by P-time Petri net is presented. The adopted approach based on a system of differences of constraint separates timing properties from behavioral ones. Furthermore the proposed method yields to the consideration of a single source shortest path problem obtained for a feasible occurrence sequence of the untimed underlying PN that can be polynomially solved thanks to the Bellman-Ford algorithm.
